title: Will the Congressional Leadership Fund report more than $145M in cash on hand at the end of Q3? Above $145M
rules: If the Congressional Leadership Fund's cash on hand is above $145 million as of September 30, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_secondary: This market resolves based on the official filing data released by the Federal Election Commission (FEC). Only the first official or non-preliminary release of the relevant statistic will be used to resolve the market, and subsequent revisions, corrections, or updates will not affect resolution.

blind.reasoning: CLF had $141.8M on hand on June 30, 2026, so it only needs about $3.2M of net growth in Q3 to clear $145M. In the same quarter of 2024 it raised $81.4M and ended with $153M, and its 2026 fundraising is ahead of that pace. The main risk is heavy September ad spending from its roughly $175M of fall reservations in a tough environment for Republicans, which could outrun what it raises.
blind.falsifier: CLF's Q3 FEC report (due Oct 15) or its own press release shows cash on hand of $145M or less as of Sept 30, 2026, because spending outpaced fundraising.

final.reasoning: The market's low price made me cut my estimate from 0.69, since traders may know more about September spending or the lack of a Q3 announcement so far. CLF still needs only about $3.2M of net growth after a record Q2, so 0.52 stays above the 0.44 ask.
